audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's phase block is templated from a favoured matchup: every stage is marked side=Cassiopeia at 2/10, which is self-contradictory, and the level chart in the content layer marks Level 6 as Cassiopeia's while its own whys[4] says Akali deletes you there.
audit.why: The content layer's prose is accurate and consistent — Cassiopeia owns levels 1-3, Akali owns Levels 4-5 through first item once Twilight Shroud and Perfect Execution are online, and it evens out at two items. The win array and the full-layer phases both disagree with that prose. Sides and ratings realigned to the prose.
audit.corrected: win[2]=Skill, win[3..5]=Akali, win[6]=Skill; full phases sides realigned and all seven whys rewritten to the real matchup. Numeric phase ratings left untouched pending a ruling on what the number means.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere for the two abilities the matchup is built on.
audit.why: Twilight Shroud is 20/19/18/17/16s and Perfect Execution is 120/90/60s. Those two numbers are what make 'wait for its downtime' actionable instead of a slogan.
audit.corrected: Shroud and Perfect Execution cooldowns now stated in the cooldown windows, the win condition and the key-interactions row.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3].why claimed 'Drop W on his approach path and Twilight Shroud stops being scary' — Miasma does nothing to Twilight Shroud.
audit.why: Miasma grounds movement abilities. Twilight Shroud is not a dash; it is an untargetable smoke, so grounding is irrelevant to it. The abilities Miasma actually answers are Shuriken Flip (E) re-cast dash and the Perfect Execution (R) dashes. Separately, while Akali is inside the shroud she cannot be selected by spells or attacks, so Twin Fang has no target at all — that is the decisive interaction of the matchup and the full layer never stated it.
audit.corrected: phases[3] now states that Twin Fang cannot select her inside the smoke; the grounding claim is redirected to Shuriken Flip and Perfect Execution, which are actual dashes.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2], dontsFull[1] and dontsFull[2] have bodies copy-pasted from unrelated entries, and the whole full layer calls Akali 'him' and 'his'.
audit.why: dosFull[2] is headed 'Win extended exchanges with E-spam' but its body is about Akali spending shroud. dontsFull[1] is headed 'E-spam unpoisoned targets at range' but its body is about Miasma. dontsFull[2] is headed "Forget R's stun wins any face-to-face" but its body is a verbatim duplicate of tradeBad.
audit.corrected: Bodies rewritten to match their headings; pronouns fixed in every string I touched.

notes: The full layer's Akali page was clearly cloned from the Aatrox page — identical phase whys, identical tradeGood/tradeBad, and Akali referred to as 'him' throughout. I fixed the pronouns only in strings I was already editing; several untouched strings (loading, breakdown.wave, breakdown.trading, report[4], report[11], dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[0].d) still say 'him'/'his' and still carry Aatrox-shaped advice. Worth a dedicated pronoun pass across cassiopeia.full.js rather than burning length budget matchup by matchup. Also: the kit file flags Cassiopeia's Twin Fang (E) as a Wind Wall-blockable projectile; Riot's description has no travel language and this looks like a tooltip-parse misfire, so I asserted nothing about it. RATINGS LEFT ALONE: phase .rating is incoherent on this page (every stage reads side=Cassiopeia at 2/10 while diff is 8/10). On the Aatrox page a favoured stage is side=Cassiopeia at 7-8/10 and on the Akshan page a losing stage is side=Akshan at 6-7/10, which reads as 'how strongly the named side owns this stage'. Under that reading the Akali numbers are simply wrong, but I did not want to guess the scale, so I fixed only the sides and the whys.
